judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is announced ('The Cash Value is equal to:') but the operators are missing, and 'C' — the difference between interest actually credited and guaranteed interest over the preceding 12 months — is an unusual deduction whose sign is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cash Value feeds 5.7 Surrender Value, 5.9 withdrawals and 9.4's lapse test, and 9.4 states the lapse trigger in Cash Value terms while 5.10 states it in Surrender Value terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Surrender Value equals Cash Value less Policy Indebtedness; two lines, no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reconciles 5.10's Surrender-Value lapse test with 9.4's Cash-Value-less-indebtedness test, so the two are arithmetically the same measure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The right to surrender 'at any time' is clear; the six-month postponement right and the exception for premiums on another policy with us are stated but OCR-damaged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.1's unconditional promise to pay the Surrender Value while the Insured lives does not mention any postponement or written request, a mismatch with this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The withdrawal limits are internally muddled — a minimum of $500 in one phrase and $25 in another, a Withdrawal Charge stated as 'A + B + $25' with 'B' undefined, and a rule that the first-year Surrender Fee is 'decreased by A divided by the Percent of Surrender Fee'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its automatic reduction of the Specified Amount under Option A must be read with 6.2's decrease mechanics and the Minimum Specified Amount in Section 1, which are not obviously aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The central lapse trigger is broken mid-sentence ('will lapse if the Surrender Value on a Monthly Due Date is not [sufficient to] pay the next Monthly Insurance Charges'), and the 60-day Grace Period's start point is not identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.4 states a lapse trigger in Cash-Value terms with no grace period, and the final paragraph of 5.10 bars lapse altogether in the first two Policy years, so three lapse rules must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice is promised 'at least 50 days before the end of the Grace Period' when the Grace Period itself is only 60 days, a numeric oddity that leaves almost no lapse-warning window as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to work with 5.10's 60-day period and 5.10(2)'s termination without value; whether notice is a condition of lapse is not answered anywhere in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Terminate without value' is stark and definite, though 'adequate premium' is not quantified except by the notice in 5.10(1).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.4 nevertheless allows reinstatement for five years after the Grace Period using values in effect at lapse, which is hard to square with termination 'without value'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deduction of 'any premium which remains unpaid' from Proceeds is clear in principle, but the amount of premium 'unpaid' during a grace period is not defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.2 already lists the adjustments to death benefits (riders, premiums, indebtedness) without mentioning this deduction, so the two adjustment lists differ.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The no-lapse guarantee is stated as an absolute for the first two Policy years, subject to a pro-rata premium test whose sentence trails off ('multiplied by the number of months since the Policy Date').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly qualifies 5.10's opening lapse rule and appears to contradict 9.4, which says the Policy 'will lapse whenever' the Cash Value margin is insufficient with no first-two-year carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical statement of reserve and minimum-value bases naming a specific table, rate and method.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.6's floor that Cash Value never be less than the state-required minimum; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short procedural right to request changes in writing; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 6.4's requirement of officer approval for changes not provided for in Section 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A heading sentence introducing the conditions for changing the Specified Amount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.12's statement that the Specified Amount may be increased or decreased as provided in 6.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions 1 and 2 turn on what is 'satisfactory to us', a discretionary standard, though conditions 3 and 4 are objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.2(4) separately conditions increases in Planned Periodic Premium on insurability, and 7.8 gives increases their own two-year contestability period; both fit rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is scrambled around 'following our approval' and the promised addition to Section 1, so the effective date rule is only inferable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2.7 points to 6.2 for the effective date of Specified Amount changes, so this fragment is the operative text for that cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain discretionary cap of one increase in any 12 months.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 3.2(4)'s cap on additional premiums; no inconsistency located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reverse-order application of decreases is stated, but the final sentence about the amount remaining in force after a requested decrease is cut off, leaving the minimum unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.9 imposes a Minimum Specified Amount floor after Option A withdrawals, which is presumably the same floor this truncated sentence intended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text survives only as fragments — a change from Option A to Option B on evidence of insurability, with 'the new Specified Amount will be the death benefit less the [Account Value]' — and says nothing about a change from B to A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2.14 and 4.2 define both options symmetrically, so the one-way change right stands out against them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any change to your Policy that is not provided for in this section' plus the no-agent-authority sentence is a familiar formula, though 'this section' could mean Section 6 or the clause itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 7.1's entire-contract clause and 6.1's writing requirement, and the two would be read together on any waiver argument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This Policy the application and any supplemental applications are the entire contract' is missing punctuation, and the consideration recital adds 'any subsequent premiums' which is not truly consideration for issuance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.1's no-coverage-until-payment rule and 7.2's Temporary Insurance Agreement both bear on what documents form the contract, so the entire-contract clause has to be squared with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The representations-not-warranties sentence is standard and its 'in the absence of fraud' qualifier is a recognised term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 7.8 incontestability, which permits contest within two years — the two together determine what the insurer may assert and when.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The later-of test is broken by OCR, and the proviso that health 'and all other conditions affecting the insurability of the Insured have remained as stated in the application' is an open-ended condition on the effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes itself 'subject to Section 7.7 - Incontestability' when incontestability is in fact 7.8 (7.7 is Misstatement of Age and Sex), and its Temporary Insurance Agreement reference sits against 3.1's no-coverage-until-payment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-item reporting list introduced by 'at least the following information', which is expansive rather than ambiguous; item 10's lapse notification is densely worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 10 overlaps with 5.10(1)'s grace-period notice without saying how the two notices relate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is truncated and rests on 'a reasonable charge as determined by us', a standard set unilaterally by one party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.5 repeats the same 'reasonable charge determined by us' formula for illustrative reports; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A right to a projection report for a reasonable charge; the sentence trails off at 'based on information supplied in ...'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 7.4's annual report; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'While sane or insane' and the two-year period are conventional, but the clock runs 'from the Issue Date', a term used but nowhere defined in this policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy elsewhere works from the Policy Date (2.6) and the Effective Date (2.7, 7.2), so the suicide clause's start date cannot be fixed from the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only fragments of the misstatement-of-age-and-sex adjustment survive, so the adjustment basis is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.2 cross-refers to '7.7 - Incontestability' when 7.7 is this misstatement clause, so the numbering of this provision is itself in issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception — no contest after two years 'unless the Surrender Value is insufficient to cover the next Monthly Cost of Insurance' — mixes contestability with lapse and would be read very differently by the two sides; 'Issue Date' is again undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across 5.10's lapse machinery and 3.4's reinstatement rights, and 7.2 cites the wrong section number for it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence two-year contest period for increases; the OCR gap does not obscure the rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves increases out of 7.8's Initial-Specified-Amount clock, which is coherent, though it inherits the same undefined start-date problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence: the Policy is nonparticipating and pays no dividends.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the cover page's 'NONPARTICIPATING' description and with the excess-interest crediting in 5.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'You may exercise every [right] provided by your Policy if: 1. There is no irrevocable beneficiary; and 2. The Policy has not been assigned' reads as an all-or-nothing suspension of every owner right on either event, which is a strong and probably unintended construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.3 says only that owner and revocable-beneficiary rights are 'subject to any assignment', and 8.4 limits only the change of beneficiary where the designation is irrevocable — both narrower than 8.1's blanket condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The change-of-ownership mechanics survive only in fragments, so the effective date of a change is not readable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.4's change-of-beneficiary rule supplies the same 'effective when signed but no effect on prior payments' formula, indicating what was intended here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four short sentences on assignment, each definite; 'not binding on us' until written notice is a familiar term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1 conditions all owner rights on the Policy 'not having been assigned', which is broader than this clause's subordination rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear default rules: beneficiary as shown on the application, Owner if none named, 'except as provided in this section'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2.4 defines the Beneficiary as named in the original application without the no-beneficiary default, and 4.1 says Death Proceeds go to the Beneficiary flat out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The survivorship rules are stated in order (beneficiary, Owner, Owner's executor or administrator) with no gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.4's opening default and with 10.1's identification of the payee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The change takes effect 'upon the date your request was signed' but has no effect on payments already made — a relation-back rule that is clear, if occasionally contested on facts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the irrevocable-beneficiary condition in 8.1 and the parallel wording in 8.2; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Almost nothing survives beyond 'You may obtain a Policy [loan] ... is the only security needed', so the loan entitlement and its limits are unstated here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.2 supplies the amount available and 9.3 the interest, so the fragment depends entirely on the sections following it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The maximum loan formula's opening is lost, leaving only the two deductions, so the base amount available cannot be read off the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the Cash or Surrender Value definitions in 5.6-5.7 and interacts with 9.4's indebtedness deduction; which value is the base is not stated anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest at 'the rate specified in Section 1', payable annually, with unpaid interest added to the loan; definite apart from the truncation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2 reduces the crediting rate on the loaned portion to the loan rate less two points, and that clause's own arithmetic example is wrong, so the two rate provisions must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition and the deduction from Proceeds are clear; the lapse sentence is an absolute ('your Policy will lapse whenever') with no grace period or first-two-year qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That absolute lapse rule sits against 5.10's 60-day Grace Period and against 5.10's express no-lapse guarantee for the first two Policy years.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence identifying who may elect an option is scrambled, and the qualification 'subject to Section 8' is undirected.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8 governs ownership, beneficiary and assignment, so the electing party under 10.1 has to be worked out from 8.1, 8.3 and 8.4 rather than from this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sum payment at the date of claim settlement; the simplest option in the section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1's payment of Proceeds and 10.2's basis-of-options rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause runs two ideas together ('either for a specified period or for a specified amount, the present value, which is equal to the Policy Proceeds') and its 4% floor sits against an accompanying table it does not identify as guaranteed.
